sources.title: Wickremasinghe, Anuradhapura Slab Inscription of Kassapa V, Epigraphia Zeylanica 1
sources.note: Direct transcript and translation. Printed pages 41 to 57; translation lines 6 to 56 covers monasteries, medical halls, tanks, study, protections, youths, care, and accounts.

sources.title: Siddham, Anuradhapura Slab Inscription of Kassapa V
sources.note: Curated inscription record and object linkage. Checked with object OB03022 and the direct Epigraphia Zeylanica transcript.

sources.title: Wickremasinghe, Two Tablets of Mahinda IV at Mihintale, Epigraphia Zeylanica 1
sources.note: Direct transcript and translation. Printed pages 98 to 113; Slab A lines 9 to 58 and Slab B lines 1 to 58 cover study, illness, accounts, work, pay, crafts, medicine, cleaning, and water.

sources.title: Siddham, Mihintale Inscription of Mahinda IV
sources.note: Curated record and full line-group translation: two 58-line Sinhala prose slabs installed by Mahinda IV, with sixteenth regnal-year preamble and monastery regulations.

sources.title: Wickremasinghe, Anuradhapura Slab Inscription of Mahinda IV, Epigraphia Zeylanica 1
sources.note: Direct transcript and translation. Printed pages 113 to 120; transcript line 44 and translation lines 41 to 45 preserve daḷdā-ge and Tooth-relic-house.

sources.title: Siddham, Anuradhapura Slab Inscription of Mahinda IV
sources.note: Curated record and translation, lines 1 to 49: same style and language as Mihintale, made months later, with land rules and Tooth-relic-house identification.

sources.title: Paranavitana, Badulla Pillar Inscription, Epigraphia Zeylanica 3
sources.note: Direct revised transcript and translation. Printed pages 71 to 100; translation sides A to D covers petition, joint sessions, family restraint, goods, tolls, transit, and redress.

sources.title: Siddham, Badulla Pillar Inscription
sources.note: Curated record: 203 lines, nearly 2,000 akṣaras, second regnal year of Siri Saṅg-bo Udā, mid-tenth-century palaeography, and Udaya identification caveat.

sources.title: Siddham, Kukurumahan-Damana Pillar Inscription
sources.note: Curated record: 73 lines in tenth-century Sinhala alphabet, eleventh regnal year of Siri Saṅg-bo, immunities for a village belonging to an Anuradhapura hospital, and ruler-attribution argument.

sources.title: Siddham, Poḷonnaruva Council Chamber Pillar Inscription
sources.note: Curated record: fourth regnal year of Abhaya Salamevan, uncertain Kassapa V or Dappula V attribution, and annual dried-ginger payment to a hospital.

sources.title: Siddham, Velmilla Slab Inscription of Sena III
sources.note: Curated record, paragraphs 1 to 5: damaged slab, eighth regnal year, elimination-based Sena III attribution, named heir, and pamuṇu immunities.

sources.title: Siddham, Kataragama Pillar Inscription of Dappula V
sources.note: Curated record, paragraphs 1 to 5: sixth regnal year, alternative circa 946 or 924 dating, Rohaṇa grant, prince Lämäni Mihind, and possible future Mahinda IV identification.

sources.title: H. W. Codrington, List of the Sovereigns of Lanka
sources.note: Older chronological reconstruction, table lines Udaya I through Mahinda V. Used only with explicit warning that its dates and numbering conflict with inscriptional identifications.

sources.title: Seshat, Anurādhapura IV polity profile
sources.note: Scholarly databank profile, general description citing K. M. de Silva pages 18 to 19: Second Lambakanna dynasty, late Anuradhapura polity, and South Indian pressures.

sources.title: Priyantha Jayasingha, Tang dynasty pottery in Sri Lanka
sources.note: Antiquity Project Gallery 80.309, printed pages 1 to 4, especially Pottery in Sri Lanka: Tang and Five Dynasties ceramics at Mantai and inland monasteries, with shipboard-storage interpretation kept tentative.

sources.title: L. Thilini Tharushi De Silva, An Investigative Study of Food Culture in Ancient Ceylon through Inscriptions
sources.note: Open University Research Sessions 2019 abstract, printed page 81: named inscriptions and foods across the first through thirteenth centuries, mostly monastic offerings; the broad chronology is explicit.

sources.title: W. M. K. Wijetunga, The rise and decline of Chola power in Ceylon
sources.note: SOAS PhD thesis repository abstract and chapter map: pre-tenth-century relations, Rajaraja occupation, Rajendra consolidation, resistance, administration, economy, society, and religion. Used for staged-transition structure, not its typographical regnal dates.

sources.title: W. I. Siriweera, Sanitation and Health Care in Ancient Sri Lanka
sources.note: University of Peradeniya repository article. Printed pages 1 to 5 cover sanitation and late Anuradhapura hospitals; page 9 covers Mihintale physicians, leech practice, staff, and remuneration.

sources.title: Zhongwu Ma and N. S. Gunawardana, The Interplay of Monastic Economy and Medical Practices in the Kingdom of Anuradhapura
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Historian 86.4, pages 258 to 276; abstract and epigraphic discussion connect grants, hospital construction, education, healthcare, and monastic economic institutions through the early eleventh century.

sources.title: Abeywardana, Bebermeier and Schütt, Ancient Water Management and Governance in the Dry Zone of Sri Lanka
sources.note: Peer-reviewed open article, sections 3.1 to 3.3 and Tables 2 to 4: tanks, water shares, ownership, settlement, and historically layered governance.

sources.title: Central Bank of Sri Lanka, Currency Museum Guide
sources.note: Official museum guide, printed page 19: eighth- to eleventh-century gold kahavanu, standing and seated figures, and alternative readings of the Nāgarī legend.

sources.title: George W. Spencer, The Politics of Plunder: The Cholas in Eleventh-Century Ceylon
sources.note: Peer-reviewed article, notes 15 and 21 to 31: earliest 993 conquest-list evidence, later chronicle authorship, 1017 problem, Chola foothold, and Polonnaruwa evidence.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Sacred City of Anuradhapura
sources.note: Authoritative heritage description: 1,300-year political and religious capital, invasion in 993, abandonment narrative, and surviving palaces, monasteries, and monuments.

sources.title: Sujantha Gunasena, Kingship in Ceylon from the fourth to the tenth century A.D.
sources.note: SOAS PhD thesis repository abstract and chapter map: political background, sources, royal titles and names, royal family and offices, consecration, the nature of rule, and relations between kingship and the Sangha.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Buddhist Meditation Monasteries of Ancient Sri Lanka
sources.note: Sri Lankan tentative-list dossier: Ritigala, Manakanda, Arankele, and Maligatenna as fifth- to tenth-century archaeological monastic sites, with preservation context.

sources.title: Trivalent, Information Preservation and Dissemination in Ancient Sri Lanka
sources.note: University of Kelaniya journal article, printed pages 34 to 36: Badulla petition, lost earlier rule, public inscription, offices, and documentary preservation.
